meta.title: Dune Universe
meta.description: A scroll-driven editorial tour through the houses, planets, music and books of Dune.

hero.title: Explore World of Dune
hero.body: Dune is a science fiction story set in a space empire far in the future. It follows Paul Atreides, heir to House Atreides, whose family is forced to leave the ocean world of Caladan and take control of the desert planet Arrakis.

about.title: About
body: A mythic and emotionally charged hero’s journey, “Dune” tells the story of Paul Atreides, a brilliant and gifted young man born into a great destiny beyond his understanding, who must travel to the most dangerous planet in the universe to ensure the future of his family and his people. As malevolent forces explode into conflict over the planet’s exclusive supply of the most precious resource in existence—a commodity capable of unlocking humanity’s greatest potential—only those who can conquer their fear will survive.

houses.title: The Great Houses
houses.body: The Landsraad holds the balance between the noble houses, the Imperium and the orders that quietly shape both. Drag the cards to read each creed.

items.name: Corrino
items.quote: Secrets do not diminish when they are spread among many ears.

items.name: Gesserit
items.quote: Survival is the ability to swim in strange water.

items.name: Harkonnen
items.quote: There is no escape - we pay for the violence of our ancestors.

items.name: Atreides
items.quote: A great man does not seek to lead. He is called to it.

items.name: House Atreides
body: A rich history for the Atreides, as well as various other titles, including the House of Pelops, and successively Lords of Tantalos, Counts of Thuestes, Counts of Aramanli and Counts Chalcedony.
Siridar Dukes of Caladan, Siridar Dukes of Arrakis, and Emperors of the Known Universe; junior titles include Barons Pelops, Barons Menelaus and Counts Gamnonides.

items.name: House Harkonnen
body: House Harkonnen was a Great House of the Landsraad. The Harkonnen capital was Giedi Prime, a heavily industrialised planet with a low photosynthetic potential.
The house was known for underhanded political tactics and for an ancient feud with House Atreides. It was typically ruled by a Siridar Baron.

items.name: The Freemen
body: The Fremen were a sub-culture of humans descended from the Zensunni Wanderers who considered the planet Arrakis their home.
They formed an integral part in the establishment of the Atreides Empire and the Jihad launched by Paul Atreides, their adopted leader.

heroes.body: The son of a great man and royal heir to House Atreides, Paul has spent his entire life being prepared for the greatness that comes with his family's name.

arrakis.title: Arrakis
arrakis.body: Arrakis was for a long time the sole source of the spice melange, the substance that makes interstellar travel possible. It sits far from the populated worlds and their trade routes.

caladan.title: Caladan
body: Caladan was the fiefdom of House Atreides and the birthplace of Duke Leto Atreides I, of Paul, and of most of the ancestors who ruled the planet before them. Their traditional seat was Castle Caladan.
After the Atreides moved to Arrakis, Count Hasimir Fenring was named Siridar-Absentia. When the house later ascended to the Golden Lion Throne, Caladan returned to direct Atreides rule.

architecture.title: Dune Architecture
architecture.body: Architects have long tried to imagine what the built world of the future will look like. Production designer Patrice Vermette had to imagine twenty thousand years ahead: a story spanning multiple planets, each with its own material logic, weather and idea of shelter.

soundtrack.title: Space Orchestra
soundtrack.body: The Dune Sketchbook runs a hundred minutes across nine tracks - an unhurried, cavernous score that treats the desert as an instrument.

tracks.title: I See You in My Dreams

author.title: Frank Herbert
body: Frank Herbert used his science fiction novels to work through philosophy, religion, psychology, politics and ecology. The thread running under all of it was a fascination with human survival and evolution.
He attracted a devoted readership, many of whom set out to read everything he wrote, fiction and non-fiction alike, and treat him as an authority on the subjects his books circle.

comics.title: Dune Comics
comics.body: Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson, with artist Dev Pramanik, adapt their prequel novel into comics for the first time - set in the years leading up to the events of Dune.
